canonical_claim: Review finding №7 is real: the receiver compares the advertised pool only on the sender, so a reservation can select a non-CA disk or a different CA pool and publish a dangling manifest or throw before byte fallback. Additionally, A receiver must compare the reservation-selected disk's CA pool UUID with the advertised pool UUID and use byte fallback for either a non-CA disk or a different pool. Additionally, After fetch reservation, a relink is allowed only when the chosen disk is CA and its pool UUID equals the advertised pool UUID; otherwise the code must invoke the existing byte-fetch fallback. Additionally, Relink can advertise pool A while reservation selects a local disk or pool B, allowing pool B to publish references to bodies that exist only in A.
